An empty argument reaches the exact Whom do you wish to force do what? response.
A target without a command takes the same half_chop usage branch.
An unresolved target emits C's NOPERSON bytes.
A target at the caster's level is rejected with No, no, no!.
C get_char_room_vis resolves self before the level comparison, producing the equal-level rejection.
The me alias follows the same self-target path.
C acknowledges before command_interpreter(vict,to_force); the room observer exposes the ordering.
The 0.<name> player-only target form resolves the connected PC and executes the harmless command.
An in-room abbreviated player name follows get_char_room_vis matching.
A LVL_GOD caster may force a lower-level connected player; only room/all require LVL_GRGOD.
A below-implementor caster sends the exact $n has forced you message to the victim before execution.
The room branch reaches only lower-level characters in the caster's room; a remote mortal is omitted.
The all branch reaches connected lower-level characters in other rooms and skips equal/higher levels.
Room/all unconditionally call act to each eligible victim, including when the caster is an implementor.
At LVL_GOD, room/all are ordinary target names; they do not enter the population loops.

The second safe NPC probe confirms the unresolved generic handoff, not a missing player message. Do not claim the NPC target class proven by the player-only force path.
